analysis:
The supplied units are documentation only: attestation.md (head text, lines 263-535; no patch shown) and identity-binding.md (patch bumping the date, adding two sections, plus base text). No executable code or coordinator logic is in the batch, so no concrete security regression is visible.

New documented behavior in identity-binding.md:
1. Same-process endpoint resumption (~lines 94-110). The provider's in-memory NodeKeyPair answers an App Attest protocol-1 resume challenge via CoordinatorClient.answerAppAttestResume (ProviderLoop+Serve.swift). The doc claims the answer is single-use, bound to the current socket and nonce, creates no local trust, extends no Apple proof lifetime, and that backend retained-proof, account and revocation checks are platform-owned. Relevant: TB-002, TB-011, T-053 (replay or stale authorization), A-003, A-015, A-016. Next pass must check that the resume answer cannot reinstate or extend a grant, and that K is never persisted.
2. Provider logout (~lines 136-146). It revokes the current saved token through a raw-bearer POST /v1/device/revoke, holds the lifecycle and single-instance locks, and notes that local deletion cannot invalidate a copy held elsewhere. Relevant: A-008, T-039, B6. The backend revocation endpoint, its persistence and rate limiting are stated to be platform-owned and are not in this batch; a later pass should confirm they exist and that revocation is hash-based and atomic.

attestation.md head text (lines 263-535) matches the existing threat model: the legacy MDM/APNs path and the App Attest path are independent; the routing gate lists App Attest as an alternative authorization; handoff rechecks the live gates; hard untrust writes a tombstone. Relevant: T-036, T-052..T-054, TB-009, TB-011. The text states the legacy MDM cohort gates (Policy.RegistrationAllowed, Policy.ProviderAllowed) but the code is not supplied.

Coverage limit: the code behind these doc claims was not reviewed, so the claims are unverified.
